Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington (“KFHPWA”) is a nonprofit health maintenance organization, duly
registered under the laws of the State of Washington, furnishing health care coverage on a prepayment basis. This
Evidence of Coverage (“EOC”) sets forth the terms under which that coverage will be provided, including the rights

enrolled under this EOC are entitled.

Important Notice Under Federal Health Care Reform
Kaiser Foundation Health Plan of Washington (KFHPWA”) recommends that each Member choose a Network
Personal Physician. This decision is important because the designated physician provides or arranges for most of the
Member’s health care. The Member has the right to designate any Network Personal Physician who participates in
KFHPWA’s Core Network and is available to accept the Member or the Member’s family members. For information
on how to select a Network Personal Physician, and for a list of the participating Network Personal Physicians, please
contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640 in the Seattle area, or toll-free in Washington, 1-800-
290-8900.
For children, the Member may designate a pediatrician as the primary care provider.
The Member does not need Preauthorization from KFHPWA or from any other person (including a Network Personal
Physician) to access obstetrical or gynecological care from a health care professional in the KFHPWA network who
specializes in obstetrics or gynecology. However, the health care professional may be required to comply with certain
procedures, including obtaining Preauthorization for specific services, following a pre-approved treatment plan, or
procedures for obtaining Preauthorization. For a list of participating health care professionals who specialize in
obstetrics or gynecology, please contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640 in the Seattle area, or
toll-free in Washington, 1-800-290-8900.
Women’s Health and Cancer Rights
If the Member receives benefits for a covered mastectomy and elects breast reconstruction in connection with the
mastectomy, the Member will also receive coverage for:
• All stages of reconstruction of the breast on which the mastectomy has been performed.
• Surgery and reconstruction of the other breast to produce a symmetrical appearance.
• Prostheses.
• Treatment of physical complications of all stages of mastectomy, including lymphedema.
These services will be provided in consultation with the Member and the attending physician and will be subject to
the same Cost Shares otherwise applicable under the EOC.
Statement of Rights Under the Newborns’ and Mothers’ Health Protection Act
Carriers offering group health coverage may not, under federal law, restrict benefits for any hospital stay in connection
with childbirth for the mother or newborn child to less than 48 hours following a vaginal delivery, or less than 96
hours following a cesarean section. Federal law does not prohibit the mother’s or newborn’s attending provider, after
consulting with the mother, from discharging the mother or the newborn earlier than 48 hours (or 96 hours as
applicable). However, carriers may not, under federal law, require a provider to obtain authorization for prescribing a
length of stay not more than 48 hours (or 96 hours). Also, under federal law, a carrier may not set the level of benefits
or Out-of-pocket costs so that any later portion of the 48-hour (or 96-hour) stay is treated in a manner less favorable
to the mother or newborn than any earlier portion of the stay.
Discussing Treatment Alternatives
While Kaiser Permanente doesn’t cover every kind of treatment or procedure (no health plan does), Kaiser Permanente
doesn’t use financial incentives or penalties that encourage doctors or other clinicians to withhold Medically Necessary
services or discourage them from discussing recognized medical alternatives with you. The only financial incentives
used are rewards for medical groups and hospitals that meet quality care measures (such as cancer screenings) and
patient satisfaction targets.
Important Resources
Visit kp.org/wa/important-resources to learn about coverage documents, other plan documents, and preventive care
schedules. You can also find information about our quality program, hospital care and safety ratings, women’s health
and cancer rights, and important health plan and pharmacy disclosures.
Case Management for Chronic Conditions
Registered nurses certified in case management offer phone-based support for managing chronic asthma, diabetes,
high blood pressure, cholesterol, or heart disease. contact 1-866-656-4183.

3. Identification Cards.

4. Administration of Evidence of Coverage.
KFHPWA may adopt reasonable policies and procedures to assist in the administration of this EOC. This may
include, but is not limited to, policies and procedures pertaining to benefit entitlement and coverage

5. Modification of Evidence of Coverage.
This EOC, including the premium, may be modified by KFHPWA upon 30 days written notice mailed to each
Contract Holder’s address, as it appears in KFHPWA’s records. Failure to receive such notice shall not affect
the modification or effective date.
To report a change of address, contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640 in the Seattle area,
or toll-free in Washington, 1-800-290-8900.
No oral statement of any person shall modify or otherwise affect the benefits, limitations and exclusions of this

6. Notices.
The Contract Holder shall notify either the Washington Health Benefit Exchange in accordance with their
guidelines or KFHPWA in writing of any changes in residence within 30 days of such change. Notices provided
for in this EOC shall be mailed to KFHPWA at its principal address and to the Contract Holder’s address as it
appears in KFHPWA’s records.
7. Compliance With Law.
KFHPWA and the Contract Holder shall comply with all applicable state and federal laws and regulations in
performance of this EOC. This EOC is governed by the laws of Washington State, except as where federal law
preempts state law.
8. Governmental Approval.
If KFHPWA has not received any necessary government approval by the date notice is required under this
EOC, KFHPWA will notify the Contract Holder of any changes once approval has been received. KFHPWA
may amend this EOC by giving notice to the Contract Holder upon receipt of approved rates, benefits,
limitations, exclusions, or other provisions. Any such rates, benefits, limitations, exclusions or provisions will
go into effect as required by the governmental agency.
All amendments are deemed accepted by the Contract Holder unless the Contract Holder provides KFHPWA

information and to provide notice describing how such information may be used and disclosed. The Notice of

www.kp.org/wa, or upon request from Member Services.
10. Nondiscrimination.

services. KFHPWA will not refuse to enroll or terminate a Member’s coverage and will not deny care based on

or health status.

I. Introduction
This Evidence of Coverage (EOC) describes the terms of enrollment, payment, and coverage under which the
Contract Holder may obtain health benefits. KFHPWA endeavors to provide and arrange for a wide range of
medical and Hospital Care.
The provisions of the EOC must be considered together to fully understand the benefits available . Words with
special meaning are capitalized and defined in Section XII. If the Member is eligible for Medicare, the Member
should review Section IV. Drugs – Outpatient Prescription as it may affect prescription drug coverage.
For benefit questions, contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640 or toll-free 1-800-290-8900.
II. How Covered Services Work
A. Accessing Care.
1. Your Provider Network is KFHPWA’s Core (Network). Members are entitled to Covered Services only
at Network Facilities and from Network Providers, except for Emergency services and for care pursuant to
a Preauthorization.
Benefits under this EOC will not be denied for any health care service performed by a registered nurse
licensed to practice under chapter 18.88 RCW, provided that: (1) the service is within the lawful scope of
the nurse’s license, and (2) this EOC would have provided coverage if the service had been performed by a
Doctor of Medicine licensed to practice under chapter 18.71 RCW.
A listing of Network Personal Physicians, specialists, women’s health care providers, and KFHPWA-
designated Specialists is available by contacting Member Services or by visiting www.kp.org/wa.
Information available online includes each physician’s location, education, credentials, and specialties.
KFHPWA also uses Health Care Benefit Managers for certain services. A current list of Health Care
Benefit Managers, is available at https://healthy.kaiserpermanente.org/washington/support/forms by
selecting the “ Health Care Benefit Managers (HCBMs)” link.
Receiving Care in another Kaiser Foundation Health Plan Service Area
If you are visiting another Kaiser Permanente service area or service area of a Health Plan affiliate, visiting
member services may be available from designated providers in that Kaiser Permanente or Health Plan
affiliate service area if the services are covered under this EOC. Services are subject to the provisions of
this EOC including, but not limited to, Preauthorization and cost sharing. For more information about
receiving visiting member services in other Kaiser Permanente or Health Plan affiliate service areas,
including provider and facility locations, contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640 in
the Seattle area, or toll-free in Washington, 1-800-290-8900. Information is also available at
www.wa.kaiserpermanente.org/html/public/services/traveling.
KFHPWA will not directly or indirectly prohibit Members from freely contracting at any time to obtain
health care Services from non-Network Providers and non-Network Facilities outside the Plan. However, if
you choose to receive services from non-Network Providers or non-Network Facilities except as otherwise
specifically provided in this EOC, those services will not be covered under this EOC, and you will be
responsible for the full cost. Amounts paid for non-Covered Services do not apply toward your Out-of-
pocket Limit.

participating Network Personal Physicians, contact Kaiser Permanente Member Services at 206-630-4640
in the Seattle area, or toll-free in Washington at 1-800-290-8900 or visit www.kp.org/wa. The change will
be effective within 24 hours of receipt of the request if the selected physician’s caseload permits. If a

5. Emergency Services.
Emergency services received at a Network Facility or non-Network Facility are covered. Members must
notify KFHPWA by calling the Hospital notification line (1-888-457-9516, as noted on your Member
identification card) within 24 hours of any admission, or as soon thereafter as medically possible. Coverage
for Emergency services at a non-Network Facility is limited to the Allowed Amount. Refer to Section IV.
for more information about Emergency services.
Members are covered for Emergency care and Medically Necessary urgent care anywhere in the world. If
you believe you are experiencing an Emergency, go immediately to the nearest Emergency care facility or
call 911. For an illness or injury that requires prompt medical attention but is not an Emergency, go to the
closest urgent care center. Examples include, but are not limited to minor injuries, wounds, or cuts needing
stitches; minor breathing issues; or minor stomach pain. If you are unsure whether urgent care is your best
option, call the Consulting Nurse Service at 1-800-297-6877 or 206-630-2244 for advice.
If you require Emergency care while traveling and are admitted to a non-Network hospital, you or a family
member must notify KFHPWA within 24 hours after care begins, or as soon as medically possible. Call the
notification line listed on the back of your KFHPWA Member ID card to help ensure your claim is
accepted. Keep all receipts and related documentation from non-Network care; these must be submitted
with any claim for reimbursement after returning from travel.
Access to non-Emergency care across the Network Service Area: Your Plan provides access to all
providers in the Network, including physicians and services at Kaiser Permanente medical facilities and
other Network Facilities throughout the state. Provider information is available at www.kp.org/wa/directory
or by contacting Member Services at 1-800-290-8900.
6. Urgent Care.
Inside the KFHPWA Service Area, urgent care is covered at a Kaiser Permanente medical center, Kaiser
Permanente urgent care center, or Network Provider’s office. Outside the KFHPWA Service Area, urgent
care is covered at any medical facility. Refer to Section IV. for more information regarding urgent care.
For urgent care during office hours, you can call your personal physician’s office to see if a same-day
appointment is available. If a physician is not available or it is after office hours, you may speak with a
licensed care provider anytime by calling 1-800-297-6877 or 206-630-2244. You may also visit
www.kp.org/wa/directory or contact Member Services to locate the nearest urgent care facility in your
Network.
7. Women’s Health Care Direct Access Providers.
Female Members may obtain women’s health care services directly, without Preauthorization, from a
general and family practitioner, physician’s assistant, gynecologist, certified nurse midwife, licensed
midwife, doctor of osteopathy, pediatrician, obstetrician or advance registered nurse practitioner who is
unrestricted in your KFHPWA Network. forcovered Services include Medically Necessary maternity care,
covered reproductive health services, preventive services (well-care), general examinations, gynecological
care and follow-up visits for the above services.
Women’s health care services are covered as if the Member’s Network Personal Physician had been
consulted and are subject to any applicable Cost Shares. If ta women’s health care provider diagnoses a
condition requiring other specialty care or hospitalization, the Member or the provider must obtain
Preauthorization in accordance with applicable KFHPWA requirements. For a list of KFHPWA providers,
contact Member Services or view the Provider Directory at www.kp.org/wa.
8. Travel Advisory Service.
The Travel Advisory Service provides recommendations for travel outside the United States. Nurses
certified in travel health advise Members regarding vaccinations or medications based on destination,
activities, and medical history. The consultation is not a covered benefit and a fee applies for a KFHPWA
Member’s first use of the service. Travel-related vaccinations and medications are generally not covered.
For more information, visit www.kp.org/wa/travel-service.

9. Process for Medical Necessity Determination.
Pre-service, concurrent, or post-service reviews may be conducted. Once a service has been reviewed,
additional reviews may be conducted. Members will be notified in writing when a determination has been
made.
First-Level Review:
First-level reviews are performed or overseen by appropriate clinical staff using KFHPWA-approved
clinical review criteria. Data sources for the review include, but are not limited to, referral forms, admission
request forms, the Member’s medical record, and consultation with qualified health professionals and
multidisciplinary health care team members.
Clinical information used in the review may include treatment summaries, problem lists, specialty
evaluations, laboratory and x-ray results, and rehabilitation service documentation. The Member or legal
surrogate may be contacted for information. Coordination of care interventions are initiated as identified.
The reviewer consults with the health care team as needed to make informed medical necessity
determination and may consult with a board-certified consultative specialist. All such consultations will be
documented in the review record. If the requested service appears inappropriate based on application of the
review criteria, the first-level reviewer will request a second-level review by a physician or designated
health care professional.
Second-Level (Practitioner) Review:
The practitioner reviews the treatment plan, when appropriate and discusses case circumstances and
management options with the attending or referring physician. The reviewer consults with the health care
team as needed to make an informed coverage decision and may consult with board-certified physicians
from appropriate specialty areas.
All such consultations will be documented in the review record. If the reviewer determines that the
admission, continued stay or service requested is not a Covered Service, a notice of non-coverage is issued.
Coverage based on medical necessity may be denied only by a physician, behavioral health practitioner
(such as a psychiatrist, doctoral-level clinical psychologist, certified addiction medicine specialist), dentist
or pharmacist who has appropriate clinical expertise related to the request under review and holds an
unrestricted license.
B. Assignment
The Member may not assign this EOC or any rights, interests, claims for money due, benefits, or obligations
hereunder without prior written consent.

D. Recommended Treatment.
KFHPWA’s medical director will determine, in good faith, the necessity, nature and extent of treatment to be
covered in each individual case. Members have the right to appeal coverage decisions (see Section VIII.) and to
participate in decisions regarding their health care. A Member may refuse any recommended services to the
extent permitted by law. Members who obtain care not recommended by KFHPWA’s medical director do so
with the full understanding that KFHPWA has no obligation to pay for, or accept liability for the outcome of,
such care.
New and emerging medical technologies are evaluated on an ongoing basis by the Interregional New
Technologies Committee, Medical Technology Assessment Committee, Medical Policy Committee, and
Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee. These committees evaluate a technology’s benefits, whether it has been
proven safe and effective, and the conditions under which its use may be appropriate. Their recommendations
inform what is covered on KFHPWA health plans.
E. Second Opinions.
The Member may obtain a second opinion from a Network Provider regarding a medical diagnosis or treatment
plan. The Member may request Preauthorization or may consult a KFHPWA-designated Specialist for a second
opinion. When requested or indicated, second opinions are covered when obtained with Preauthorization or
when provided by a KFHPWA-designated Specialist.
Coverage is determined in accordance with the Member's EOC; coverage of a second opinion does not
guarantee coverage of any services or treatments recommended as a result of that opinion. Preauthorization for
a second opinion does not authorize the Member to return to the physician providing the second opinion for any
additional treatment. Services, drugs, and devices recommended or prescribed as a result of the consultation are
covered only if otherwise included as Covered Services under the EOC.
F. Unusual Circumstances.
In the event of unusual circumstances such as a major disaster, natural disaster (e.g., earthquake, wildfire,
hurricane or tornado), epidemic, pandemic, terrorism, war, riot, civil insurrection, government acts, changes in
applicable law, disability of entities providing services to KFHPWA, disability of a large share of personnel at a
Network Facility, complete or partial destruction of facilities, and labor dispute, KFHPWA will not be liable for
administering coverage beyond the limitations of available personnel and facilities.
In the event of unusual circumstances such as those described above, KFHPWA will make a good faith effort to
arrange for Covered Services through available Network Facilities and personnel. KFHPWA shall have no other
liability or obligation if Covered Services are delayed or unavailable due to unusual circumstances.
Additionally, under these circumstances, if you have an Emergency Medical Condition, call 911 or go to the
nearest Emergency department as described under “Emergency Services” in the “Accessing Care” section, and
we will provide coverage and reimbursement as described in that section.

G. Utilization Management.
“Case Management” means a care management plan developed for a Member whose diagnosis requires timely
coordination. All benefits, including travel and lodging, are limited to Covered Services that are Medically
Necessary and set forth in the EOC.
KFHPWA may review a Member's medical records to verify the delivery and coverage of services and items.
Based on a prospective, concurrent, or retrospective review, KFHPWA may deny coverage if, it determines
that services are not Medically Necessary. Such determination are based on established clinical criteria and may
